stories.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
stories.takeaway: Mouse and organoid experiments identify an IgA–DMBT1 pathway that restrains colonic epithelial proliferation and colorectal tumor susceptibility.
stories.what_happened: Researchers compared IgA-deficient mouse models, oral IgA supplementation, epithelial cultures, proteomics and targeted CRISPR screens; DMBT1 signaling emerged as a mediator of epithelial growth control.
stories.why_it_matters: Adds a direct epithelial homeostasis function to mucosal IgA beyond its established role in microbial binding.
stories.caveat: Evidence is largely from mice and reductionist cultures; human prevention or treatment benefits have not been established.

stories.title: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
stories.takeaway: A tissue-interfacing microchannel approach offers a route to protein sampling without destructive tissue removal.
stories.what_happened: A Nature Communications engineering study describes maintaining patent microchannels in living soft tissue using topographical mismatch for protein-biopsy applications.
stories.why_it_matters: Highlights a potentially useful tissue–device interface strategy for longitudinal biomolecular monitoring.
stories.caveat: Clinical reliability, tissue-specific performance and longer-term biocompatibility need validation; the source does not establish routine clinical use.

stories.title: Immortalized intestinal telocytes support stem cell niche function in vitro
stories.takeaway: An intestinal telocyte model offers a tractable mesenchymal component for studying epithelial stem-cell niches in vitro.
stories.what_happened: A Cellular and Molecular Gastroenterology and Hepatology study reports immortalized intestinal telocytes that support stem-cell niche function in culture.
stories.why_it_matters: Addresses the need for experimentally accessible stromal niche components in intestinal culture and organoid systems.
stories.caveat: Immortalization and in-vitro culture may alter native telocyte biology; physiological generalizability requires further testing.

stories.title: A human gut–BBB–brain microphysiological model for studying Alzheimer's disease
stories.takeaway: A multi-tissue microphysiological platform links gut, blood–brain barrier and brain compartments for experimental neurodegeneration research.
stories.what_happened: A Lab on a Chip paper describes a human gut–blood–brain barrier–brain microphysiological model developed for Alzheimer's disease studies.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates opportunities and engineering challenges in studying cross-organ communication with interconnected human tissue models.
stories.caveat: A model platform cannot by itself establish causal gut–brain mechanisms or predict clinical disease progression.

stories.title: A microfluidic mother machine for high-throughput single-cell analysis of human leukemia T cells
stories.takeaway: A CFD-optimized microchannel array permits long-term observation of non-adherent T-cell growth and division at single-cell resolution.
stories.what_happened: Investigators designed continuous-perfusion microchannels and tracked leukemia T-cell proliferation across generations, reporting slightly asymmetric division and size-control behavior.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates how channel geometry and nutrient supply can enable controlled, time-resolved single-cell phenotyping.
stories.caveat: Demonstrated in leukemia T cells; broader primary immune-cell applications and throughput trade-offs need evaluation.
